question.problem:
Consider the rectangle $C$ in the plane with vertices $(0,0),(2,0),(2,1)$ and $(0,1),$ and the region $D$ bounded by $C.$ According to Green's theorem, 

$$
{∮}_{C}(y\operatorname{sin}⁡y-{x}^{2}y)\,dx+(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\,dy={∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

Calculate the function $f(x,y).$
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14223852/assets/8d57fb7f6b8e2e822a11f11a0267994c449c37b43df167a8d48ab8036854b8dd.png)

We have that $P(x,y)=y\operatorname{sin}⁡y-{x}^{2}y$ and $Q(x,y)=x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}=\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y\operatorname{cos}⁡y-{x}^{2},\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x}=\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y\operatorname{cos}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}(y\operatorname{sin}⁡y-{x}^{2}y)\,dx+(x\operatorname{sin}⁡y+xy\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}[\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y\operatorname{cos}⁡y-(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y\operatorname{cos}⁡y-{x}^{2})]\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\operatorname{sin}⁡y+y\operatorname{cos}⁡y-\operatorname{sin}⁡y-y\operatorname{cos}⁡y+{x}^{2})\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}A\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(x,y)={x}^{2}.$
